First, understand the problem: DDP relies on collective communication operations (like allreduce) that are inserted automatically by DDP during the backward pass. These collectives are called in the same order on all ranks. If some ranks skip a conditional branch that contains a forward computation that leads to a backward computation (and thus a collective), then the ranks that skip it will not call the corresponding collective, while the others will. This causes a mismatch: some ranks are waiting for a collective that others never call, leading to a hang.

More specifically: DDP uses "bucket allreduce" where gradients are bucketed and allreduced in the order of backward computation. If a conditional branch is taken on some ranks but not others, the backward pass on those ranks will not include the gradients for the parameters in that branch. DDP expects all ranks to participate in the same set of allreduce calls. If a rank skips a branch, it might not call the allreduce for the bucket containing those gradients, causing other ranks to hang waiting for that allreduce.
